effective.acceptance: The report's trace table has one row per requirement of the Mantle specification's Mantle Transaction section (fields, hash, arithmetic, fee, validation, execution), in the document's order, each with a file:line in the unit or an explicit 'not in unit' / 'needs external evidence'. Every confirmed code finding has a new test in logos-blockchain-core or logos-blockchain-ledger that fails on 0.3.0 for the divergence it names. Prose-only findings are marked as such. The target implementation is unchanged.
effective.context:
Logos Blockchain is a Rust workspace (edition 2024, toolchain 1.99.0 pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.lock committed). Package names carry a `logos-blockchain-` prefix the directory names lack; the `name` field of each crate's Cargo.toml is authoritative. The audited ref is the release tag 0.3.0 (commit 1da2d9d69a80452cf6b5d0e68304762d510c8a6c); record the resolved commit in the report. The specification in the prompt is one section of the Bedrock v1.1 Mantle specification LIP as published in the logos-lips repository at commit fddc2c1 (the 2026-10-08 Bedrock snapshot); the Operations, Mantle Ledger and Appendix sections are audited by their own briefs. The Appendix's Test Vectors for the Mantle transaction hash are in that other brief's section, but the hash is defined here; cite the vectors as 'needs external evidence' only if the core fixtures do not already carry them.

The section defines the Mantle transaction: its fields, the transaction hash, the arithmetic rules (overflow, units), the transaction fee (gas price, execution gas, storage gas, who pays), validation (what makes a transaction valid before execution) and execution (the order operations are applied and when a transaction fails as a whole).

Where the section lives in the code:
- core/src/mantle/transactions/ (package `logos-blockchain-core`): mod.rs the transaction type, hash.rs the transaction hash, gas.rs the fee computation, codec.rs the serialisation, states.rs and verification_helper.rs the validation states, verified_ops.rs, thresholds.rs, builder.rs, errors.rs, genesis_tx.rs.
- core/src/mantle/traits/ (mantle_tx.rs, signed_mantle_tx.rs, preverified_mantle_transaction.rs, hashable.rs, storage.rs): the traits that define what a transaction exposes to the ledger. core/src/mantle/gas.rs: gas constants. core/src/mantle/batch.rs: transaction batches. core/src/mantle/fixtures/hash.rs: hash test fixtures.
- ledger/src/mantle/mod.rs and src/gas_and_fees.rs (package `logos-blockchain-ledger`): transaction-level validation and execution against the ledger, fee charging.

Running tests: the gate runs the unit's packages with cargo-nextest, which is what CI uses (`.github/workflows/code-check.yml` runs the whole workspace that way; the whole workspace is too large for this container, so the gate is narrowed to the unit). `cargo nextest run --locked -p <package> --all-features` runs one package; `cargo test --locked -p <package> --all-features -- <filter>` works too. `.config/nextest.toml` marks a unit test slow after 30 s and kills it after 2 min. ZK proof dependencies come as prebuilt circuit crates (`lbc-*-sys` with the `prebuilt` feature) and the verifier links rapidsnark statically, so the first build compiles C++ and takes a while; nothing needs a running node, docker, or downloaded circuit files. New proof tests go in the owning crate's tests/ directory or as a `#[cfg(test)]` module file under src/ named by finding id; core/src/mantle/fixtures/ shows how transactions and ledgers are built in tests. Treat code comments that cite a spec paragraph as claims to check.
